body: Process: (1) Search everywhere - all countries and industries - for the lowest price relative to long-term earnings power (he used P/E vs history, and P/E vs growth). (2) Buy at 'maximum pessimism': when news is worst and selling is indiscriminate. (3) Diversify across many bargains, because some cheap stocks are cheap for good reason. (4) Sell when a holding's price approaches fair value or a much better bargain appears (he typically held ~4-5 years). (5) Use his cycle ladder - pessimism, skepticism, optimism, euphoria - to judge where a market is. Indian application: years of extreme pessimism (2001-03 post-KP crash, Oct 2008-Mar 2009, Aug 2013 rupee crisis, Mar 2020) all offered P/Es near 11-17x and market cap/GDP near or below 60-75%, followed by 15-30%+ annual returns; a staged buying plan keyed to those valuation levels is the individual's version. Risks: value traps; acting at 'maximum pessimism' requires cash and nerves on hand before the crash.
title: Templeton: maximum pessimism, global bargain search
